adjudications.reason: A 20-minute sample is dominated by three-point shooting variance.

attach.why: In a 20-minute half a handful of threes swing the total; a team's 3P% well above its shot-quality expectation regresses, so first-half totals should be priced on shot quality, not the hot hand.

adjudications.reason: Blowouts and foul-and-free-throw endgames change a player's minutes and shot volume; the blowout input existed but was not linked.

attach.why: Lopsided games empty the starters' minutes early; rebuilt from the model's OWN margin forecast (never the spread), blowout probability is the main downside branch of every player counting stat.

adjudications.reason: Scheme-versus-scheme matchups were modelled at sport level but not attached to the side markets.

attach.why: A dominant pass rush against a weak line ends drives and shortens the favourite's margin; the matchup term is the rush rate for versus the line's sack rate allowed.
Explosive pass offences against thin secondaries produce large margins that efficiency averages understate.
Run-heavy favourites against weak fronts convert leads into clock; margin distributions skew toward key numbers.
Option and tempo offences compress possessions and transfer variance to the underdog, changing cover probability at constant rating gap.

adjudications.reason: Turnover luck regresses and moves totals.

attach.why: Short fields from turnovers inflate points scored; a team's recent turnover margin beyond its fumble-recovery expectation regresses, so totals built on raw scoring carry a luck premium.

adjudications.reason: A team total depends on that offence against this defence, not league averages.

attach.why: Style clash sets how many possessions this offence gets and how explosive they are.
Explosive-pass allowed rate converts directly into this team's points when its quarterback is the strength.

adjudications.reason: Quarterback status changes early-game scripting.

attach.why: A backup quarterback changes the opening script and first-half pace; timestamped confirmation is the point-in-time input.

adjudications.reason: Period scoring is a team-strength problem too; the totals blueprint lacked rating inputs.

attach.why: Opponent-adjusted offence sets expected points per drive in the period.
Opponent-adjusted defence sets the opposing points per drive in the period.

adjudications.reason: Short periods amplify turnover luck.

attach.why: One early turnover decides a quarter; regressing turnover luck separates repeatable offence from noise in 15-minute sample.

adjudications.reason: Skill-position availability was catalogued but unattached.

attach.why: A starting receiver or back out redistributes targets and carries; replacement quality sets the stat shift.
Injury news has no reliable official feed in college football, so timing and source matter more than the designation.

adjudications.reason: Role share is the volume driver of every player stat.

attach.why: Target, carry and snap share translate team volume into player volume; share changes after injuries are the main source of line error.

adjudications.reason: No input described the distribution of season outcomes (CFP/conference) from schedule and rating uncertainty.

attach.why: Season outcomes are order statistics over a schedule; the simulated distribution, not the point rating, prices playoff and conference markets.

adjudications.reason: Score state affects strikeouts only through when the starter leaves; the hook input models that.

attach.why: Run differential and pitch count drive the early hook that truncates strikeout opportunity.

adjudications.reason: Count outcomes need a distribution, not a mean.

attach.why: A plate-appearance simulation produces the full distribution of hits, walks and earned runs from matchup probabilities.
Counts are over-dispersed; ignoring that mis-prices the tails of ladder thresholds.

adjudications.reason: Same mechanism as strikeouts: the starter's exit time.

attach.why: Exit time bounds the number of batters faced and therefore every count stat.

adjudications.reason: Score state matters through plate appearances and late substitutions.

attach.why: Lineup slot and game script set plate appearances; pinch-hitting and blowout substitution cut them.

adjudications.reason: Home runs are rare events; the distribution and per-PA simulation matter.

attach.why: Per-PA home-run probability, compounded over expected PAs, gives the any-HR probability; park, wind and pitcher enter per PA.
Barrel-driven hitters have heavier tails than a constant per-PA rate implies.

adjudications.reason: RBI and run opportunities depend on lineup context and game script.

attach.why: Slot, teammates on base and score state set the opportunity count.

adjudications.reason: Starter-versus-lineup matchups were catalogued but not attached to the winner market.

attach.why: The lineup's handedness mix against the starter shifts run expectancy by several percent.
Starter pitch mix against the lineup's pitch-type weaknesses changes strikeout and contact quality.
Confirmed-lineup strikeout rate by handedness is the market-free matchup summary available after lineups post.

adjudications.reason: First-inning outcomes are batting-order and top-of-lineup exposure problems.

attach.why: The first three batters, not the whole lineup, decide the first inning.

adjudications.reason: Single-inning outcomes are extremely noisy.

attach.why: BABIP luck in the starter's recent first innings regresses; raw first-inning ERA overstates persistent skill.

adjudications.reason: First-five markets depend on how deep the starter goes and the times-through-order penalty.

attach.why: Third time through the order raises run expectancy materially, so the starter's expected depth sets the first-five mean.

adjudications.reason: Starters' strand luck distorts small samples.

attach.why: ERA-minus-FIP gaps from stranding luck regress and mis-price first-five runs.

adjudications.reason: Extra-innings and delay markets are event-probability contracts: tie-after-nine distribution and weather timing, not a luck regression on skill.
No input described the season simulation distribution.

attach.why: Division, wildcard and win-total markets are tails of a schedule simulation with injury and rating uncertainty.

adjudications.reason: Leader races are max-of-N order statistics; none was catalogued for baseball.

attach.why: The probability a player finishes first is the probability his final total exceeds every rival's; correlations and games remaining set it.

adjudications.reason: Resting policy of clinched teams is a distinct mechanism for lineup-participation markets.

attach.why: Clinched or eliminated teams rest regulars and call up prospects; the policy is manager-specific and timestamped by announcement.

adjudications.reason: Reference-class base rates exist for off-field events.

attach.why: Transaction markets are priced from historical frequency by calendar window; deadline proximity drives it.

adjudications.reason: Margin distributions depend on style clash.

attach.why: Scheme clashes widen or narrow the margin distribution around the same expected spread.

attach.why: Franchise-sale, relocation and rule-change markets are priced from reference-class frequencies and announcement calendars.
